experiment_description: Central concept and process-demonstration experiment: implement a free-space induced-coherence nonlinear interferometer intended to reconstruct the spatially varying polarization of an undetected telecom-wavelength idler field by measuring only its visible correlated signal partner. A continuous-wave single-mode 532 nm pump laser pumps two identical periodically poled lithium niobate nonlinear sources, Q1 and Q2, each with crystal dimensions 1 mm × 1 mm × 2 mm, operated for type-0 non-degenerate SPDC producing signal photons at 810 nm and idler photons at 1550 nm. Signal and idler from Q1 are separated at dichroic mirror DM1. The idler from Q1 is relayed through a 4f imaging system with lenses fI1 = fI2 = 75 mm; at the Fourier plane a vortex wave plate/q-plate with topological charge m = 2 imposes a transverse-momentum-dependent polarization transformation on the idler. A half-wave plate HWP3 after the q-plate is used at 0° or 45° to select the horizontal or vertical idler polarization projection before overlap with the idler mode associated with Q2. The pump is relayed with lenses fP1 = fP2 = 75 mm and recombined toward Q2 by DM2. The Q1 signal is relayed with fS1 = fS2 = 75 mm, the Q1 and Q2 signal fields are recombined at a beam splitter, and lens fk = 150 mm Fourier-transforms the signal field to an sCMOS camera. Two 810 ± 10 nm spectral filters suppress background and reject the idler field. The camera records one image per second. No direct spatially resolving detector is placed in the 1550 nm idler arm, and no cryogenic or vacuum environment is reported. The target of the procedure is to determine whether the spatially varying Jones parameters of the undetected idler vector beam—local horizontal amplitude α(r), vertical amplitude β(r), and relative phase φ(r)—can be inferred from induced single-photon interference in the 810 nm signal field over the camera-resolved transverse beam profile, using the transverse-momentum correlations of the SPDC photon pairs. The spatial scope is the far-field camera image of the signal beam, corresponding through SPDC momentum correlations to the q-plate-structured idler transverse momentum plane; the demonstrated reconstructions cover the circular beam region inside camera fields of about 1000 × 1000 pixels for phase-shifting holography and about 1500 × 1400 pixels for off-axis holography.

undetected_telecom_vector_field_reconstr.description: Whether the described induced-coherence visible-readout procedure produced a spatially resolved reconstruction of the undetected 1550 nm idler vector field’s horizontal amplitude, vertical amplitude, and relative phase over the beam profile.

experiment_description: Multi-frame phase-shifting digital holography characterization of the undetected vector beam using the same induced-coherence interferometer. The central mechanism is that a 1550 nm idler field from Q1 receives a spatially varying polarization transformation from an m = 2 vortex wave plate/q-plate but remains undetected; after idler overlap at Q2, which-source indistinguishability converts the local idler polarization projection into 810 nm signal interference visibility. The optical hardware consists of two identical 1 mm × 1 mm × 2 mm PPLN nonlinear crystals pumped by a continuous-wave 532 nm single-mode laser, type-0 non-degenerate SPDC at 810 nm signal and 1550 nm idler, 75 mm focal-length relay lenses fP1, fP2, fI1, fI2, fS1, fS2, a 150 mm Fourier lens fk before the sCMOS camera, and 810 ± 10 nm filters before detection. HWP3 is set to 0° to measure the horizontal idler projection α(r) and to 45° to measure the vertical idler projection β(r). For each projection, a piezoelectric actuator with nanometre-scale positioning applies four relative interferometric phase steps θ′ = 0, π/2, π, and 3π/2; one camera interferogram is acquired per phase step, so eight images are used for the two-projection Jones reconstruction. For each camera pixel corresponding to a signal transverse momentum qS and correlated idler component qI, the local interference amplitude is evaluated as A_qI = 2*sqrt([I_qS(3π/2)-I_qS(π/2)]^2 + [I_qS(0)-I_qS(π)]^2)/(I_qS(0)+I_qS(π/2)+I_qS(π)+I_qS(3π/2)), where I_qS(θ′) is the recorded signal intensity at phase step θ′. With HWP3 at 0°, A_qI is interpreted as α_qI; with HWP3 at 45°, A_qI is interpreted as β_qI. The relative phase is evaluated pixelwise as φ_qI = arctan((I_qS(3π/2)-I_qS(π/2))/(I_qS(0)-I_qS(π))). The spatial scope is the camera-resolved far-field signal image covering approximately 0–1000 pixels in x and 0–1000 pixels in y, with the circular beam area used for the reconstructed amplitude and phase maps; the measurement compares both polarization projections over the same transverse field of view.

psdh_max_polarization_projection_visibil.description: Maximum reconstructed visibility in the phase-shifting holography maps for the horizontal and vertical polarization projections of the undetected idler vector field.

experiment_description: Single-shot off-axis holography characterization and quantitative comparison with phase-shifting holography for the same induced-coherence vectorial reconstruction concept. A continuous-wave 532 nm pump drives two identical 1 mm × 1 mm × 2 mm PPLN SPDC sources Q1 and Q2 producing 810 nm signal and 1550 nm idler photons. The Q1 idler is structured at the Fourier plane of a 75 mm/75 mm 4f relay by an m = 2 vortex wave plate/q-plate and then projected by HWP3 at 0° or 45° before overlap with the Q2 idler mode; the idler is not directly detected. The Q1 and Q2 signal fields are recombined at a beam splitter, spectrally filtered by two 810 ± 10 nm filters, Fourier-transformed by fk = 150 mm, and recorded on an sCMOS camera at one image per second. For off-axis holography, no piezo phase stepping is used; instead, a small angular offset between the interfering 810 nm signal fields produces spatial carrier fringes. One interferogram is recorded for each polarization projection, giving two images total for the two-projection vector-field reconstruction. The recorded intensity has the off-axis holographic form I(r)=|EO(r)+ER(r)|^2, where EO(r) and ER(r) are the object and reference signal fields. The Fourier transform is filtered to isolate one displaced first-order term, that term is shifted to the origin, and an inverse Fourier transform gives a complex field whose modulus gives the local projection amplitude and whose argument gives the phase. The spatial scope is the camera-resolved far-field signal image covering approximately 0–1500 pixels in x and 0–1400 pixels in y, evaluated over the reconstructed circular beam region and compared with the phase-shifting reconstruction over its corresponding region of interest. The quantitative comparison evaluates amplitude reconstruction quality, background level inside the region of interest, signal-to-noise ratio, and phase-map degradation area; the paper does not provide more detailed mathematical definitions for these comparison metrics.

oah_amplitude_reconstruction_quality_inc.description: Relative increase of the amplitude reconstruction quality obtained with off-axis holography compared with phase-shifting digital holography for the undetected vector-beam reconstruction.

oah_background_level_reduction_vs_psdh_p.description: Relative reduction of the background level within the reconstruction region of interest for off-axis holography compared with phase-shifting digital holography.

oah_snr_enhancement_vs_psdh_percent.description: Relative enhancement of the signal-to-noise ratio for off-axis holography compared with phase-shifting digital holography in the vectorial undetected-light reconstruction.

oah_phase_degraded_area_fraction_percent.description: Fraction of the reconstructed field area over which the off-axis holography phase reconstruction is locally degraded.
